newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish leftist rebels attack Islamist prison van.
newsitem.headline: Turkish leftist rebels attack Islamist prison van.

text.p: Turkish leftist guerrillas exploded a car bomb and opened fire on a Turkish prison van on Friday in an apparent attempt to kill eight Islamist convicts being taken to court, security officials said.
Three gendarmerie police and an inmate were wounded when the bomb was set off by remote control by a roadside in the arid province of Kirsehir.

"It would seem that the aim was to kill those inside the van," a security official told Reuters. He said a flag of the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front (DHKP-C) and cartridge cases from Kalashnikov rifles were found on a hill 40 metres (120 feet) from the car bomb.
The prisoners were being taken to Ankara where they face the death sentence in a trial for allegedly forming an armed group with the intention of changing Turkey's secularist constitution.

The eight were among 41 people originally sentenced to 15 years each for an Islamist arson attack that killed 37 people, most of them members of a liberal Moslem sect, in 1993. An appeals court later ordered retrials and tougher sentences.
Turkish courts sometimes issue death sentences although nobody has been executed since the early 1980s.

Anatolian news agency earlier said the attack appeared to be an escape attempt. The security official said gendarmerie police escorting the prison van in different vehicles had prevented any bid by the prisoners to flee.
"A young gendarme who was driving the van deserves credit. He brought the van to an orderly halt despite being injured by the bomb," the official said.
Left-wing attacks on Islamists are rare. "It is the first time I have heard of something like this in Turkey," the official said.
Local officials in the town of Tokat blamed the DHKP-C for a car bomb explosion near government offices there on July 17.
The leftist group's most sensational attack in recent years was the killing of a leading industrialist and two of his colleagues at their high-security headquarters last year.

The group is a splinter from the now defunct Dev Sol (Revolutionary Left) which killed dozens of people, mostly members of the security forces, in the 1970s and '80s before breaking up early this decade.
Police were on alert at large mosques throughout the country on Friday to halt any Islamist protests against government plans to curb Moslem religious education.
At least 20 people were detained at Istanbul's 16th century Beyazit mosque, witnesses said.
